Philosophy: project management = context management — concurrent context must never be silently lost.

All findings from the 2026-07-03 concurrency audit are resolved or explicitly waived: atomic claim test-and-set, bounded lock-wait retry, singleton-file locking, ID-allocation TOCTOU guard, stale-lock takeover race. Parallel multi-agent stress (mutations, claims, config writes) preserves item and history integrity with zero silent lost updates.

## Charter
Capability epic for concurrency & multi-agent safety, created from the 2026-07-03 concurrency audit. pm is agent-first: many agents mutate one git-backed workspace in parallel, so locking, claim semantics, id allocation, and singleton-file writes must be safe by construction. Audit verdict: data integrity held under all parallel stress (no corruption, no history drift) — the five children are availability/atomicity gaps, not corruption bugs.

## Delivery order (dependency-informed)
1. pm-2muu lock-wait retry (in progress, implemented uncommitted) — foundation: gives every mutation a bounded wait.
2. pm-8t5x claim test-and-set (in progress, implemented uncommitted) — relies on the item lock; with 2muu it is a true atomic test-and-set.
3. pm-zwib stale-lock takeover race — related to 2muu (its removal cap bounds but does not fix the race).
4. pm-khdq create/copy ID allocation TOCTOU (silent item overwrite — worst blast radius).
5. pm-bgcu singleton-file (settings/schema/session/checkpoints) lock-free read-modify-write.

## Verification bar
Every child closes with parallel-stress evidence recorded via pm test / notes (the audit's empirical repros re-run green): N-parallel mutations self-heal, claims are exclusive, no lost config writes, no id collisions.

author: maintainer-agent
message: Anchor concurrency to the simulation harness, harness identity, merge conformance, and the scale outcome

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Multi-agent concurrency assessment 2026-07-25, covering the branch-merge and fleet-coordination halves together because they are usually confused for one problem.

Merge safety is structurally complete and shipped: field-aware item merge, history union and re-anchoring, JSON merge for config and schema, a committed merge fence installed by init, storage-integrity validation, strict-exit history verification, and transaction-scoped garbage collection. What is not yet proven is that it stays complete under arbitrary divergence, which is why continuous multi-branch merge conformance (pm-76dnfg) exists as a property suite with a zero-conflict acceptance bar rather than as more point fixes. The open architectural question - whether field-level three-way merge is sufficient at thousands of agents or whether conflict-free replicated state is required - is deliberately held as a decision (pm-2sbj8p) blocked on that property suite plus the fault simulator, because it should be answered by measured conflict rates rather than by preference.

Coordination is where the real gap was. Ownership safety is solved: claim is an atomic test-and-set, id allocation and stale-lock takeover races are closed, and cross-branch id collisions are addressed by configurable entropy plus duplicate detection. But safety is not efficiency. Thousands of agents ranking the same queue independently converge on the same head, waste claim attempts, and leave the critical path unstaffed - none of which any existing gate or benchmark measures. Fleet allocation (pm-3oqjnc) is filed to own that, with claim remaining authoritative so advice can never corrupt ownership, and with the explicit requirement that a fleet of one reproduces today's ranking exactly.

Three open races remain tracked (config singleton read-modify-write, id allocation TOCTOU residual, stale-lock takeover residual) and they are deliberately the acceptance targets of the deterministic fault simulator rather than being fixed blind. That ordering matters: a race fixed without a reproducer is a race that returns.

The measurement gap worth naming: every concurrency claim in this epic is currently argued from code review rather than from a contention benchmark. Claim and lock throughput at scale (pm-lvyd) is the missing instrument, and it blocks the allocation work for exactly that reason - allocation cannot be shown to improve anything until collision waste is measurable.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text:
Multi-agent convergence program

Correctness layers are distinct. Local mutation uses per-item or per-stream compare-and-swap with atomic temp-write, fsync, rename, and lock ownership tokens. Cross-process coordination uses bounded waits, jittered retries, stale-lock fencing, and observable contention. Branch convergence uses semantic merge drivers over canonical field and append-only event representations. Cross-workspace federation waits on the evidence-backed convergence ADR rather than assuming three-way merge scales forever.

Every operation carries a stable event id, author/harness provenance, base version, causal predecessors where needed, and an idempotency key. Conflicts are returned as structured plans with both candidate values and safe retry instructions; no last-writer-wins path may silently discard independent work. Singleton workspace state follows the same transactional rule as items.

Verification spans deterministic scheduled interleavings, property tests, crash injection, branch fan-out and merge, mixed-version readers/writers, thousands-of-agent claim storms, and restore after partial failure. Invariants include no lost update, no duplicated durable id, no broken history chain, no unowned live lock, deterministic replay, and identical convergence for equivalent event sets.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Fleet write-contention probe, 2026-07-30, recorded so nobody re-derives it. Twenty-four concurrent processes appended a comment to ONE item in a fresh sandbox workspace. Result: 24 of 24 exited 0, 24 of 24 comments are present, the item stream holds 25 history entries (1 create + 24 comment_add), zero lost updates, zero lock_conflict escapes, empty stderr. Wall clock 3.035 s for 24 serialized writes, so roughly 8 committed mutations per second against a single contended item.

Reading: the per-item lock is correct under 24-way contention and the immutable record is complete. The open scale question is not correctness but that ~8 writes/sec/item is a hard serialization ceiling, which is a throughput property of one-file-per-item storage rather than a race. Do not file a race item from this probe; the races that remain open are the singleton-file ones (config read-modify-write) and id reservation, which this probe does not exercise.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Read-path concurrency measured 2026-07-30 (evening), and the finding is that the read path now takes a global write lock.

Every pm next and pm context serve appends to the context usage ledger, and the append is guarded by one workspace-wide lock named for the ledger, with a three second wait budget. Twelve concurrent pm next calls completed in 5,145 milliseconds of wall clock against 1,013 milliseconds for a single serial call, so roughly a 2.4-fold speedup where twelve independent reads should be near-linear. No entries were lost and no line in the ledger was unparseable, so this is a throughput ceiling rather than a correctness failure, and the write is correctly wrapped so a lock timeout degrades the signal instead of failing the read.

Two structural facts make it worth recording here rather than only on the cost item. The lock is taken on a read command, so the concurrency characteristics of reads are now governed by a write path, and a fleet sized for reads will contend on a resource that reads did not previously touch. And the entry itself scales with the corpus: a context serve records one row per open item, 315 today, while its sibling caps at 200, so per-read lock hold time grows with the workspace rather than staying constant.

This complements rather than duplicates the earlier concurrency evidence on this epic. The 24 concurrent annotation writers on one item that all succeeded were mutation writers contending on an item lock. This is read commands contending on a single shared workspace lock, which is the first case on this epic where reads serialise against each other. The cost and scaling of the ledger are tracked as their own issue, and the correctness of what it records is tracked separately again.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Fresh-clone fence state, measured 2026-08-02 on pm 2026.8.2. A clone of a git-backed tracker carries the committed .gitattributes naming five pm merge drivers but none of the clone-local git config driver definitions, so until pm merge install runs, every pm data file in that clone merges under git's default line-based strategy. Detection exists and is better than the AGENTS.md prose implies: pm validate --check-storage-integrity reports merge_driver_configuration status missing with all five missing_keys, and pm health --summary names merge_driver_configuration_missing:5 in its warnings. What does not exist is a verdict: the check declares required:false, the workspace verdict is ok:true, and health exits 0, so the aggregate an agent is routed to describes an unprepared clone as healthy. Routed here as capability evidence; the consolidation is pm-bq0ii8 and the grammar rule is ruling K on pm-pbyu.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Concurrency claims must be tested as algebra, not as scenarios. A merge scenario test asks whether one merge lost data; the property that matters at fleet scale is whether the combination operation is a function of its inputs alone. Running the identical branch pair in both directions separates the two immediately — union collections came back byte-identical, every scalar came back as whichever side happened to be merging — and it costs about twenty lines of shell. The corollary is the reason this went unnoticed: the existing randomized property varied only a union collection and compared it sorted, so it exercised precisely the half of the field space that cannot fail. When a property suite is written from the same intuition as the implementation, it inherits the implementation's blind spot; the way out is to enumerate the classes the implementation itself distinguishes and require the property to name each one.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Fresh multi-agent merge evidence 2026-08-04: pm validate reports merge fence and driver healthy, zero pending merge decisions, zero history drift, zero storage-integrity errors, and no active dangling references. Eight focused merge/lock suites passed 120 tests, including merge-safety installation, driver policy, reconciliation, receipts, CLI registration, command behavior, item-lock coverage, and lock GC. GitHub #889 exposes a separate recovery-guidance gap under pm-fbrz7p; the underlying merge primitives passed.

message: Conflict-free multi-agent operation depends on durable append-only history and deterministic replay

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Multi-agent convergence design: represent every mutation as an idempotent operation with stable event identity, causal parents, actor/session provenance, previous hash, and deterministic field semantics. Claims are leases for coordination, not ownership of history; append-only comments/evidence merge freely, set-like tags and typed edges use identity-aware add/remove operations, scalar conflicts retain both proposals plus an explicit resolution event, and terminal transitions require causal preconditions. The Git merge driver must parse and merge PM records by schema rather than line order, preserve both branch histories, reject hash gaps or duplicate event identities, and produce the same current state independent of branch merge order. Test N-branch fan-out/fan-in, simultaneous create/update/close/release, rename and delete-like compensating events, clock skew, retries, partial writes, interrupted rebase, stale leases, and adversarial duplicate IDs. Scale through per-item logs, content-addressed snapshots, incremental indexes, optimistic compare-and-append, and bounded conflict summaries; measure conflict rate, lost-update rate, convergence time, merge amplification, and context freshness at thousands of agents. Never use force ownership or silent last-writer-wins to make a test green.

author: harness:codex

patch.value: Make concurrent, retried, cross-process, cross-worktree, and cross-branch mutations converge deterministically without losing any acknowledged state
Thousands of agents can coordinate through one tracker without silent last-writer-wins loss, global serialization, or manual history repair

Parallel branches, immutable per-item streams, claim leases, and field-aware merge drivers are already production-critical; remaining duplicate-id, scalar-conflict, fresh-clone fence, and fleet-throughput gaps compound nonlinearly as agent count grows.

message: Add strategic outcome metadata for the multi-agent safety programme

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Multi-agent convergence design: every mutation carries a globally unique event identity, actor provenance, logical time, previous hash, payload hash, and schema version. Merge semantics are field-specific: append-only sets for comments, notes, tests, and evidence; logical-identity upserts for relationships; explicit conflict receipts for competing scalar state; deterministic ordering and replay; short renewable claims as coordination hints rather than truth. Validate N-branch commutativity, associativity, idempotence, replay equivalence, interrupted writes, duplicate delivery, clock skew, and conflict recovery. SDK transactions, CLI adapters, merge drivers, and hosted checks must consume the same algebra.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Scale boundary: retain per-item immutable streams for local reasoning while building disposable, reproducible indexes and graph summaries for portfolio queries. Indexes may be compacted or rebuilt; evidence streams may not. Cross-branch reconciliation must expose what was merged, rejected, superseded, or still conflicted, and must never silently choose by filesystem order.
